I'll work through each chapter draft carefully, applying the gate test to every potential structural issue.

**Ch 006 Draft Analysis:**

The jump from "We've got a job!" to "The joint venture has really begun" to "Julius P. Hersheimmer!" is compressed — in the source, Tommy says the joint venture line, then separately both realize Julius, then they discuss taking a taxi. In the draft: `"The joint venture has really begun," said Tommy. "Julius P. Hersheimmer!" / "We never told Mr. Carter about hearing from him," said Tommy.` Tommy is attributed twice in consecutive lines with no intervening speaker — a minor seam but parseable. More importantly, the exclamation "Julius P. Hersheimmer!" is unattributed — in the source it's Tommy who voices it, but in the draft it follows Tommy's previous sentence without a speaker tag. A reader could reasonably parse this as a continuation from Tommy. Not a genuine confusion.

The "it" in "you really has the devil of a time getting anything out of *it*" — in the source this refers to "the Government" which Tuppence just mentioned. In the draft, the Government reference was cut: Tuppence says "but when we want more—" then "It will be waiting for you" then "Yes, but—you know one really has the devil of a time getting anything out of it!" The antecedent "it" (= the Government) has been dropped. A reader genuinely cannot tell what "it" refers to here.

**Ch 007 Draft Analysis:**

"They repeated the wheeze ad lib; a couple of fruitless calls later—Tommy's impersonation had supplied many a Christian name and slammed many a door—they lunched briefly" — "slammed many a door" is odd but parseable as metaphor for concluding visits. The authorized cut of Mrs. Sweeny/Miss Wheeler canvass montage means the reduced detail here is expected.

The draft says `"We'll just get down to it. London first. Note the addresses of any women in or near town while I put on my hat."` then immediately `They set out for the first address, The Laurels.` — "The Laurels" appears without prior establishment in the draft. Checking: in the source ch 007, The Laurels is introduced as "The Laurels, Glendower Road, N.7." In the draft, the list is referenced but The Laurels is not named before "They set out for the first address, The Laurels." A reader does understand this is the first address on the list, so it's not genuinely confusing — they can infer it. Gate test: less ornamented, not confused.

The "it" problem in Ch 006 is the clearest structural damage.
